slot.brief: Use the inclusion–exclusion principle on a survey/venn-type data set to find |A∩B∩C| or |exactly two sets|.

stem: In a survey of 72 people, everyone uses at least one of three apps. The numbers using A, B and C are 42, 38 and 35; the pairwise intersection sizes are 18, 16 and 15. How many use exactly two apps?

verdicts.working: By inclusion–exclusion, the triple intersection is 72 − 115 + 49 = 6. Exactly two = (18 + 16 + 15) − 3(6) = 31.

working:
$n(A\cap B\cap C)=72-(42+38+35)+(18+16+15)=6$. Exactly two $=(18+16+15)-3(6)=31$.

Independent check: By inclusion–exclusion, the triple intersection is 72 − 115 + 49 = 6. Exactly two = (18 + 16 + 15) − 3(6) = 31.
solution:
By inclusion–exclusion, the number using all three apps is
$$n(A\cap B\cap C)=72-(42+38+35)+(18+16+15)=6.$$
The pairwise intersections count each person using all three three times, so exactly two apps are used by $(18+16+15)-3(6)=31$ people.
